museum.network.openMuseum.transition.tit: A permanent record beyond the website
museum.network.openMuseum.transition.goa: The public repository is the bridge to an on-chain Museum record. The Fall 2026 goal is to give every admitted policy, decision, accession, provenance statement, rights record, preservation event, and correction a verifiable commitment and append-only lineage.

museum.network.proposition.title: The 6529 Network Museum
museum.network.proposition.metadata: The 6529 Network Museum is a permanent collection of digital art held for the benefit of the 6529 Network and the public.
museum.network.proposition.intro: The 6529 Network Museum is a permanent collection of digital art held for the benefit of the 6529 Network and the public. It collects, preserves, studies, and shares art from the history of internet-native culture.
museum.network.proposition.principle: The Collection is held for long-term stewardship, research, interpretation, and public access. Accessioned works are intended to remain in the Collection.
museum.network.proposition.art.title: Works held and studied
museum.network.proposition.collection.bo: The permanent Collection contains works that have been formally accessioned by the Museum. Casey Reas and Magnum Photos are represented by completed gifts.
museum.network.proposition.collection.ac: Keys and Gates is the first Meme Card-funded acquisition program. Its selected photographs are current acquisition work and remain separate from the permanent Collection while acquisition and accession proceed.
museum.network.proposition.scholarship.b: The Museum publishes artist studies, collection essays, acquisition writing, object entries, and records that help visitors look closely and follow the relationships among works.
museum.network.proposition.public.title: A museum open to the public
museum.network.proposition.public.body1: Anyone can visit the Museum online. The Collection, its artists, and its scholarship are available for public study and conversation.
museum.network.proposition.public.body2: The 6529 Network holds the Collection for the public commons. Museum governance, rights, provenance, and preservation records explain how that responsibility is carried out.
museum.network.proposition.working.title: How the Museum works
museum.network.proposition.working.intro: The Museum records its decisions, custody, rights, and collecting work in public. These records support the art and the people who study it.
museum.network.proposition.today.title: The Museum today
museum.network.proposition.today.body1: The Museum has an accessioned Collection, adopted collecting policies, TDH-weighted decisions, dedicated Ethereum custody, and a public institutional record.
museum.network.proposition.today.body2: Major collecting and policy decisions are made through the Network's governance process. The public record documents those decisions and the Museum Safe holds the accessioned works.
museum.network.proposition.today.collect: The accession register defines the permanent Collection. Accessioned works are held in the dedicated Museum Safe, with Ethereum custody and transfers independently verifiable.
museum.network.proposition.today.governa: The Network uses TDH-weighted voting for major collecting and policy decisions. Adopted effects and proposals awaiting adoption remain separate in the public record.
The repository is the Museum's current canonical institutional record. Its rules, records, revisions, and history are version-controlled and open to inspect.
museum.network.proposition.next.title: The next stage
museum.network.proposition.next.intro: The Museum's next stage will connect Network governance, the institutional record, and Ethereum execution through three linked parts.
museum.network.proposition.next.decision: Approved Museum decisions will have a form that can be independently verified on Ethereum and in the institutional record.
The Museum Safe will follow valid Network decisions through technical custody controls.
museum.network.proposition.next.executio: Valid decisions will have a reliable path to an authorized Ethereum action, including an acquisition, transfer, or mint.
museum.network.proposition.next.conclusi: Together, these parts connect governance, institutional memory, custody, and execution.
museum.network.proposition.permanence.bo: The Museum is built to survive changes in websites, software, operators, signers, and service providers.
Long-term care joins Ethereum state to content-addressed records, preserved media and software, rights and provenance evidence, and migration paths.
Future stewards should be able to reconstruct the Collection, its decisions, and its institutional history from these records.

museum.network.acquisitionPrograms.title: Acquisition programs
museum.network.acquisitionPrograms.descr: The Museum's acquisition page explains its collecting frameworks, named programs, acquisition methods, and accession status.
museum.network.acquisitionPrograms.lead: The Museum uses two standing frameworks: gifts from donors and acquisition programs funded by Meme Card proceeds. Every acquisition is documented separately, from proposal through accession.
museum.network.acquisitionPrograms.frame: Two ways the Museum builds the Collection
Gifts are offered by donors. Meme Card-funded acquisition programs use the proceeds and terms of a named Meme Card to acquire or commission work under the program's rules.
Donors offer works to the Museum. Accepted and accessioned gifts become part of the permanent Collection.
Casey Reas, Magnum Photos, and Vera Molnár

The Museum has accepted and accessioned gifts of work by Casey Reas, five Magnum photographers, and Vera Molnár, in collaboration with Martin Grasser. Each gift has its own curatorial and accession record.
A named Meme Card can fund an acquisition program. The card's proceeds and adopted terms support the program's scope, selection, and acquisition work.
Keys and Gates is the first Meme Card-funded acquisition program. Selected photographic works are being prepared for acquisition and accession.
museum.network.acquisitionPrograms.metho: A framework describes how the Museum organizes collecting. An acquisition method describes how a particular work is obtained. Accession records the formal decision to add it to the permanent Collection.
A donor gives the Museum a specified work or group of works.
The Museum buys a specified work, directly or through an approved acquisition program.
The Museum commissions a new work or acquires it when it is first minted.
The Museum may also receive a work through an estate, an exchange, or a transfer from another holder.
A work enters the permanent Collection after formal accession. Offers, selections, mints, and wallet transfers remain earlier steps in the record.
museum.network.acquisitionPrograms.curre: The named acquisitions below sit within their collecting framework and retain their own status.
museum.network.acquisitionPrograms.terms: A program sets a collecting scope. An acquisition is a specific work or group of works obtained through that program. Accession is the final act that adds each accepted work to the permanent Collection.
museum.network.acquisitionPrograms.detai: This program record gives the scope and terms for the acquisitions it produces. Each work keeps its own status in the Museum's record.

museum.network.research.artistVeraDescri: Molnár used grids, lines, circles, and letters to test how small changes alter a composition. Her work moved between drawing, painting, plotter output, and computer code.
museum.network.research.artistMartinDesc: Martin Grasser works with typography, drawing, code, and generative systems. Themes and Variations develops the letters N, F, and T as both image and structure.
museum.network.research.workThemesDescri: Themes and Variations turns the letters N, F, and T into blocks, bars, intervals, and texture. In #210, a small F and repeated T forms sit within the project's six-by-six grid.

museum.network.research.systemDescriptio: Seven works by Casey Reas show how a system can produce images with sharply different structures, textures, and tempos.
museum.network.research.magnumDescriptio: Five photographs made between 1952 and 2016 approach conflict through borders, sacred and domestic space, smoke, ruins, and uncertain aftermaths. Accession 6529NM.2026.002 is recorded as Conflict at Its Edges, five photographs from Magnum Photos 75.
museum.network.research.keysGatesDescrip: Sixteen photographs selected through Keys and Gates examine access, control, permission, and exit. They have not yet been minted, acquired, or accessioned and are not in the permanent Collection.
museum.network.research.magnumDisplayBas: These All Rights Reserved works are shown as part of the Museum’s permanent Collection. The Museum’s credited institutional display position does not transfer copyright or create a general reproduction licence.
museum.network.research.artistCaseyDescr: Reas works with software, generative systems, moving image, and print. His practice asks how rules, machines, and institutions condition what an image can be.
museum.network.research.artistTowellDesc: Towell's photographs are grounded in long engagement with family, land, migration, and political violence, often at the scale of daily life.
museum.network.research.artistSamanDescr: Saman examines conflict and political upheaval through the environments, gestures, and ambiguities that remain outside official narratives.
museum.network.research.artistHugoFazDes: HugoFaz photographs the figure, the shore, and the conditions of public visibility. Two works were selected through Keys and Gates.
museum.network.research.artistNasimDescr: Nasimghanizadeh's selected photograph uses architecture and controlled movement to examine the limits placed on freedom.
museum.network.research.artistShamsDescr: Shamspranto's selected work addresses the visual memory of Bangladesh's Liberation War and the public life of historical images.
museum.network.research.workPreProcessDe: A close reading of Reas's unfinished forms, layered procedures, and the visual evidence of a system still in motion.
museum.network.research.workPhototaxisDe: Light, motion, and accumulated marks turn a biological response into a changing field of digital behavior.
museum.network.research.workBarAmDescrip: Micha Bar-Am's photograph holds protest, religious space, and spectatorship within one compressed public scene.
museum.network.research.workMeloniDescri: Lorenzo Meloni photographs Palmyra after destruction, where archaeology, propaganda, and the present occupy the same ground.
museum.network.research.workNoKeyDescrip: A Keys and Gates photograph in which a lit passage is divided by a gate-like screen.
museum.network.research.workCostOpenDesc: A landscape photograph that connects entry with reservation, capacity, time, and cost.
museum.network.research.magnumOrganizati: Founded in 1947, Magnum Photos is a photographer-owned cooperative whose history shaped modern documentary photography and the circulation of photographic authorship.
